Stock assessment results {#sec-stock-assess-results}
------------------------

### Uncertainty ensemble {#sec-structural-uncertainty-analysis}

Of the 100 ensemble model runs, 80 met the gradient convergence criteria $\leq 1.0 \times 10^{-4}$ of which 62 had positive definite Hessians. The 80 models were retained in the ensemble for management advice; of the 20 models that failed ten failed the convergence gradient criterion and ten were incomplete. For the 62 positive definite Hessian fits, 100 correlated inverse-Hessian draws were propagated jointly by the multivariate delta method; 18 Near-PDH fits contribute structural uncertainty only. Estimation uncertainty is therefore incorporated into the statistics for management advice, but is not complete for all models.

The retained models and uncertainty results can be explored in the [interactive HTML viewer](https://pacificcommunity.github.io/ofp-sam-bet-2026-ensemble/bet-2026-ensemble-interactive-viewer.html).

The planned and retained model numbers by uncertainty category are shown in @fig-ensemble-design-retention. More models were retained at the two higher $\tau$ values, which assign less weight to tag data, and when reporting-rate adjustments were excluded during the mixing period. Otherwise, retained models were distributed across the levels of each uncertainty component. Equal total model weights prevented these differences in retention from giving greater influence to categories containing more retained models.

The influence of each uncertainty component on the management quantities across the ensemble of models is displayed in @fig-management-uncertainty-continuous-axes-steep-M, @fig-management-uncertainty-discrete-axes-tau-mix and @fig-management-uncertainty-discrete-axes-tag-rep-effcrp. Natural mortality and tag mixing were most influential on the spread of the ensemble.

The trajectories of $SB$/$SB_{F=0}$, spawning potential, fishing mortality and recruitment for each of the 80 models are displayed in @fig-ensemble-individual. Fifteen central model estimates had recent $SB$/$SB_{F=0}<0.2$. Ribbon plots combining structural uncertainty and the available estimation uncertainty are provided in @fig-ensemble-est-uncert-ribbon.

### Analyses of stock status {#sec-stock-status-analysis}

There are several ancillary analyses related to stock status that are typically undertaken on the diagnostic model including dynamic Majuro and Kobe analyses and fisheries impacts analyses.

We do not present every ancillary result for every model. This section relies mainly on the equal-model-weight ensemble summaries in @tbl-manage-quant, @tbl-stock-status-refs, @tbl-ref-points and @tbl-est-uncertainty, the time-series uncertainty in @fig-ensemble-est-uncert-ribbon, and the dynamic Majuro and Kobe plots in @fig-time-dynamic-kobe-majuro.

### Majuro and Kobe plots and comparisons with reference points

Most of the combined uncertainty distribution lies in the Kobe and Majuro areas corresponding to a stock that is not overfished and not undergoing overfishing, although the distribution extends into less favourable categories (@fig-combined-kobe-majuro-status). The equal-model-weight mixture assigns an 18.6% probability to recent depletion below the LRP, a 17.3% probability to $SB_{recent}/SB_{MSY}<1$, and a 24.1% probability to $F_{recent}/F_{MSY}>1$ (@tbl-stock-status-refs). The category probabilities are printed directly within the corresponding plot areas to make the uncertainty allocation explicit, following the general panel-percentage presentation used by @kim_quantitative_2025; that study is cited for the visualisation approach, not as evidence for the tuna assessment results.

The dynamic Majuro and Kobe trajectories for both the diagnostic model and the annual ensemble median show declining stock status and increasing fishing mortality since the 1950s, with fishing mortality increasing more strongly from the late 1960s (@fig-time-dynamic-kobe-majuro). The ensemble median remains more optimistic than the diagnostic model, consistent with the diagnostic model being near the pessimistic edge of the ensemble.

### Fishing impact and time-dynamic MSY

Dynamic MSY declined from relatively high values early in the assessment as the fishery expanded and the age composition of removals changed, and was broadly between approximately 120 and 150 thousand t in recent decades (@fig-dynamic-msy). Recent catches were generally near or below the corresponding dynamic-MSY series, although both quantities vary annually and this comparison is not a replacement for the ensemble reference-point results.

Estimated fishery impact increased in all regions, with the greatest terminal impact in Region 2 and substantial impacts in Regions 3 and 4 (@fig-impact-region). At the stock-wide scale, associated purse-seine fisheries made the largest single contribution to the increase since the 1990s; longline and miscellaneous fisheries also contributed materially. The attribution depends on the diagnostic-model spatial and fishery structure and should be interpreted as a decomposition of that model's estimated impact.

### Yield analysis

The diagnostic-model equilibrium yield curve was relatively flat near its maximum (@fig-yield). The fishing-mortality multiplier associated with recent fishing was close to, but slightly above, the multiplier producing the maximum equilibrium yield, while the corresponding equilibrium yield remained close to MSY. Management quantities derived model by model from the yield analysis are summarised in @tbl-manage-quant and @tbl-ref-points; the ensemble median $F_{recent}/F_{MSY}$ was 0.838 after incorporating structural and available estimation uncertainty.

### Catch-based projections {#sec-projection-results}

Under fishery- and quarter-specific catches fixed at their 2022--2024 means, the ensemble projected recovery in both depletion and spawning potential after 2024 (@fig-projection-stock-trajectories). Across the 800 model--recruitment realisations, median depletion increased to 0.355 in 2030, 0.517 in 2040 and 0.545 in 2054 (@tbl-stock-projections). In 2030, 5.2% of realisations were below the 0.20 LRP and 6.9% were below the 2012--2015 depletion objective; none of the realisations was below either benchmark in 2040 or 2054. Median spawning potential increased from 523.1 thousand t in 2030 to 720.6 thousand t in 2054. These are conditional projections under the specified recent-catch scenario, not forecasts of future catches or management action, and their intervals include recruitment variability but not Hessian parameter uncertainty.
